Katanga Mining Ltd Appoints New Chief Operating Officer Amid Growth Initiatives

LUBUMBASHI, Democratic Republic of the Congo, June 14 — Katanga Mining Ltd, a leading producer in the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s copper and cobalt sector, announced Friday that it has appointed Jean-Paul Mukendi as its new Chief Operating Officer, effective immediately.

The company said in a statement that Mukendi, a Congolese national with over 20 years of experience in the mining industry, will be responsible for overseeing daily operations at its flagship mining complex in Kolwezi. He succeeds François Mbemba, who is retiring after more than a decade of service.

“We are pleased to welcome Jean-Paul Mukendi at a pivotal time for the company,” said Katanga Mining Ltd Chief Executive Officer Sarah van Dijk. “His expertise in large-scale mining operations and his deep understanding of the local context will be invaluable as we continue to expand our production and deliver value to stakeholders.”

Mukendi previously held senior operational roles at several mining companies in Central and Southern Africa. In his new role, he will focus on operational efficiency, workforce development, and the implementation of new sustainability initiatives, the company said.

Katanga Mining Ltd’s Kolwezi operation is among the largest integrated copper and cobalt producers in Africa, employing more than 5,000 people, the majority of whom are local residents. The company’s latest quarterly results showed output of 52,000 tonnes of copper and 7,800 tonnes of cobalt, representing a year-on-year increase of 9% and 12% respectively.

Industry analysts say the appointment signals Katanga’s intent to strengthen its operational leadership as global demand for battery metals continues to rise.

“With the push for electric mobility and renewable energy storage, companies like Katanga are under pressure to ramp up production responsibly,” said Emmanuel Tshiswaka, an independent mining analyst based in Kinshasa. “Bringing in someone with Mukendi’s track record on both efficiency and community engagement is a smart move.”

The Congolese Mining Workers’ Union welcomed the appointment, calling for continued investment in worker training and local hiring. “We look forward to working closely with Mr. Mukendi to ensure that job opportunities and safety standards remain priorities,” said union spokesperson Mireille Kasongo.

Katanga Mining Ltd stated it remains committed to supporting local communities and adhering to the highest safety and environmental standards as it pursues further growth in the region.
